declared_purpose: Maintain persistent task plans, findings and progress for complex agent work; restore selected project context after interruptions or compaction. Optional features provide explicitly requested same-project history counts or bounded replay, structured progress tracking and host-dependent completion gating.

data_operations.source: Agent task context, research and tool observations
data_operations.data_scope: Requirements, goals, decisions, findings, source references, actions, changed files, validation results and errors
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected task directory: task_plan.md, findings.md and progress.md; subsequent reads return to the calling agent
data_operations.condition: Explicit planning-workflow requirements. Recovery reads the selected files and requests git diff --stat; research and error recording depend on the task.

data_operations.source: Packaged templates, initialization arguments, date and generated identifiers
data_operations.data_scope: Planning-file skeletons; task-name-derived dated plan identifiers; optional mode, nonce, attestation and gate state
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Project-root files in legacy mode or .planning/<plan-id>/; named initialization also updates .planning/.active_plan
data_operations.condition: Explicit initializer invocation. Autonomous/gated initialization adds sidecars, resets the block counter and removes stale gate-ledger state; named plans can inherit the project mode.

data_operations.operation: Resolve, inspect and persist plan selection
data_operations.source: PLAN_ID, PWF_PLAN_ROOT, .planning/.active_plan, directory entries and modification times
data_operations.data_scope: Plan identifiers, paths, existence and filesystem metadata; listing additionally derives phase counts
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Resolver/listing caller; explicit switching persists the shared .planning/.active_plan pointer
data_operations.condition: Shared resolvers reject invalid explicit selectors and multiple unpinned plans. Listing and switching are explicit helper calls. Some other helpers use different resolution logic, identified below.

data_operations.source: Resolved task_plan.md and caller-supplied phase/status arguments
data_operations.data_scope: Existing plan text and one phase status; temporary lock ownership metadata
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Resolved task_plan.md, temporary replacement file and .pwf-locks/phase-status.lock/.owner; result goes to caller
data_operations.condition: Explicit phase-status helper invocation; performs a locked read-modify-write. Intentional changes require re-attestation where attestation is enforced.

data_operations.operation: Compute, store, inspect or delete attestation
data_operations.source: Selected task_plan.md, existing attestation and optional .nonce
data_operations.data_scope: Full plan bytes for SHA-256; stored digest, plan/storage paths and optional nonce for display
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: .attestation beside a named plan or .plan-attestation in legacy mode; display output remains with caller
data_operations.condition: Explicit attest/show/clear invocation, or automatic attestation during autonomous/gated initialization. Clear deletes the attestation, not the plan.

data_operations.operation: Consume hook identity and Stop metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Session, agent and prompt identifiers; Stop payload including stop_hook_active
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local wrapper/interpreter memory and derived environment bindings; Stop payload is forwarded to the local completion checker
data_operations.condition: Registered standalone lifecycle events after eligibility checks. Identifiers are validated; session/agent identity is hashed for cache keys. This does not itself read session transcripts.

data_operations.operation: Read selected planning inputs for injection
data_operations.source: Selected task_plan.md, attestation, plan/project .mode and progress or ledger files
data_operations.data_scope: Plan up to 4 MiB; attestation up to 128 bytes; progress up to 1 MiB; up to 32 ledgers of 256 KiB each; mode tokens
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local injector memory; the shell implementation additionally uses snapshot files
data_operations.condition: Activated injection path after selection, containment and applicable session-attachment checks. Rejected snapshots stop injection. Autonomous/gated PreToolUse currently reads the plan before returning silently.

data_operations.data_scope: Turn start: first 50 plan lines and last 20 progress lines; legacy PreToolUse: first 30 plan lines. Smart mode substitutes selected goal/current-phase/next-step sections, active phase and recent decisions. Plan/progress views are capped at 64/32 KiB.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Hook caller/model context through stdout or additionalContext; no direct network recipient is implemented here
data_operations.condition: Successful selected-plan injection. Attestation mismatch blocks body injection; autonomous/gated modes require attestation and suppress per-tool context. If ledger-summary.sh is absent, autonomous/gated turn-start output falls back to the raw progress tail. PreCompact emits diagnostics and the stored digest rather than plan text.

data_operations.operation: Stage and delete temporary input copies
data_operations.data_scope: Python ledger-summary path writes the full bounded plan and ledger contents; other Python plan/progress snapshots stay in memory
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ledger.* directories under XDG_CACHE_HOME/pwf-snapshots, HOME/.cache/pwf-snapshots, or the temporary-directory fallback; local ledger-summary subprocess
data_operations.condition: Autonomous/gated turn-start injection with ledger-summary.sh present. Cleanup attempts unlink/rmdir on success or failure; physical erasure and crash cleanup are not established.

data_operations.source: Session/agent/prompt identity, selected plan path, rendered view and completion counts
data_operations.data_scope: Hashed session/view identifiers, turn markers, checked-item and completed-phase counts; standalone turn cache stores prompt identity
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local pwf-pretool, pwf-turn and pwf-prog cache directories
data_operations.condition: Usable cache and identity enable suppression; recovery/compaction clears applicable view state. Regression checks compare counts and may emit the plan path, lost counts and a heuristic suggestion of another writer.

data_operations.source: Caller event, summary, agent, phase and file-list arguments; existing ledgers and current UTC time
data_operations.data_scope: Global tick, timestamp, sanitized agent, phase, event, bounded free-text summary and file paths
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Resolved ledger-<agent>.jsonl; temporary .ledger_lock; acknowledgement to caller
data_operations.condition: Explicit ledger-append invocation. Existing ledgers are read to determine the next tick. Summary truncation/control-character handling does not redact sensitive content.

data_operations.operation: Infer and return structured progress summaries
data_operations.data_scope: Entry and phase counts, first active phase heading, filename-derived agent labels and last alphabetic event; summary/files/timestamp fields are omitted from output
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Direct caller, or injector progress context
data_operations.condition: Explicit summary invocation or autonomous/gated injection. The active heading is free text from the plan despite the header's broader no-free-text claim.

data_operations.operation: Evaluate completion and persist gate state
data_operations.source: Plan phase markers, plan/project .mode, Stop JSON, ledger line counts and gate sidecars
data_operations.data_scope: Derived complete/in-progress/pending counts, active phase heading, block count and previous ledger count
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller/host advisory or block-decision output; .stop_blocks and .gate_last_ledger beside the plan
data_operations.condition: Default checks are advisory. Gate blocking requires effective gated mode, an active phase, no recursive Stop, remaining block capacity and progress since a previous block. Markdown commands are not executed.

data_operations.operation: Discover and filter local Claude/Codex session records
data_operations.source: Claude project JSONL stores; CODEX_SESSIONS_DIR or ~/.codex/sessions; CODEX_THREAD_ID
data_operations.data_scope: Filenames, mtimes, sizes and recorded cwd/session metadata. Codex discovery examines metadata across substantial rollout files before selecting same-project records; Claude also examines unknown/foreign candidates to establish project identity.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local catchup process; foreign/unknown Claude transcripts are excluded from replay, with opaque-label notices in replay mode
data_operations.condition: Only explicit --metadata or --replay reaches discovery, and main first requires a root planning filename. Bare/--no-history execution returns before history discovery. Scope is project-wide rather than the selected named plan.

data_operations.source: opencode.db resolved from XDG_DATA_HOME, OPENCODE_DATA_DIR or the user data directory
data_operations.data_scope: Schema, same-directory session IDs/times, planning-write tool inputs and subsequent part JSON containing text, commands, paths and outcomes
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Read-only SQLite connection and local catchup-process collections
data_operations.condition: Explicit history mode and OpenCode installation-path dispatch. Excludes the newest session, finds a previous planning update, then collects later parts across relevant previous sessions.

data_operations.operation: Infer unsynced activity and emit aggregate metadata
data_operations.source: Selected session messages or OpenCode parts
data_operations.data_scope: Full JSONL messages are parsed locally; text, tool inputs and result annotations are collected to derive post-update entries. Metadata output contains runtime and aggregate count only.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local catchup memory; aggregate report to caller
data_operations.condition: --metadata, a recognized planning-file update and subsequent eligible entries. The boundary is inferred from planning basenames/tool events; Claude and OpenCode update detection does not require a successful write outcome.

data_operations.source: Same-project eligible history after the inferred planning update
data_operations.data_scope: Claude/Codex: last 15 entries, text excerpts up to 300 characters and up to four tool summaries; commands may contribute 80 characters, paths and short error excerpts. OpenCode: last 100 formatted parts. Payloads receive byte caps, digests and nonce framing.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Explicit replay caller; subsequent forwarding or persistence by that caller is not implemented here
data_operations.condition: --replay. Entry instructions require explicit user approval; the CLI itself trusts the mode flag. Framing and truncation do not redact credentials or personal data within excerpts.

data_operations.operation: Inspect local environment and exercise injection for diagnostics
data_operations.source: Working directory, OS name, canonical paths, plan resolution, attestation presence, install directories and injector output
data_operations.data_scope: Environment/install paths, diagnostic status, output size and wall-clock latency
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Diagnostic caller; injector also performs its normal snapshot/cache operations
data_operations.condition: Explicit plan-doctor invocation. It invokes userprompt injection once for classification and again with output discarded for timing; the second invocation still reads inputs and updates applicable state.

potential_excess.data_scope: Transcript bodies, command/path strings and tool-result excerpts materialized while calculating metadata counts
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local session-catchup process memory; no corresponding transcript disclosure in metadata output
potential_excess.condition: --metadata with eligible JSONL history or OpenCode parts
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The explicit metadata outcome is aggregate availability/counts, not replay. Content-rich extraction is an implementation choice shared with replay.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the project and planning-update boundary, classify eligible subsequent entries and count them.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Add a metadata-specific streaming/counting path; avoid building transcript collections, result annotations and formatted excerpts. For SQLite, retrieve only fields needed for eligibility/counting rather than complete part JSON where feasible.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve project filtering, update-boundary and eligibility semantics, including required text-prefix/length checks and runtime/count output.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full bounded plan and ledger contents, including ledger summaries, file paths and timestamps omitted from the resulting summary
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Python injector's pwf-snapshots/ledger.* disk directory outside the project, then the local ledger-summary.sh subprocess
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Consistent structured progress output is required; writing all raw inputs to another disk location is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Produce entry/phase counts, active heading and last event per agent from validated, consistent inputs.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Calculate the summary from verified in-memory snapshots, or stage only the necessary projection. Retain full-plan hashing in memory where needed for attestation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep existing bounds, project containment, snapshot consistency, summary semantics and fail-closed handling. Current deletion attempts reduce lifetime but do not eliminate the additional persistence boundary.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full selected task_plan.md, up to 4 MiB
potential_excess.condition: Autonomous/gated PreToolUse that ultimately emits nothing, or PreCompact that emits only diagnostics and the recorded digest
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These paths require selection/mode checks or a compaction notice. The full plan read is a redundant action on those paths, rather than extra fields in a required emitted payload.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate selection and applicable admission checks; suppress autonomous/gated per-tool output; emit the compaction reminder and stored digest when applicable.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Evaluate securely read mode state before taking the plan-content snapshot; use a selection-and-attestation-metadata path for PreCompact.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve containment, session isolation, mode-floor rules, cache resets and refusal behavior. Do not apply this reduction to paths that inject or verify plan content.

potential_excess.data_scope: Completion state from an unselected root plan, or task-specific ledger data routed into another plan
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: check-complete.ps1 caller/Stop decision; ledger files selected by helper-local resolution
potential_excess.condition: Without an explicit PlanFile, check-complete.ps1 falls back to root after a rejected explicit selector. PowerShell ledger resolution ignores PWF_PLAN_ROOT and unpinned ambiguity. Shell ledger-append falls back to root when the shared resolver refuses ambiguity.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry document explicitly requires recovery and writes to remain within the selected task and to stop on rejected or ambiguous selection.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read, summarize or append only the task's selected planning state.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use one shared resolver contract in all helpers, honor both selectors, explicitly distinguish ambiguity/refusal from legacy fallback, and refuse operations when selection is unresolved.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep legitimate legacy-root use when no selector or named-plan ambiguity applies; preserve explicit caller-selected PlanFile behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second read of selected planning inputs and repeat snapshot/cache activity
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local injector memory, snapshot storage and applicable caches
potential_excess.condition: plan-doctor invokes userprompt injection again solely to measure latency
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Diagnostic classification and latency are required outcomes; two injector executions are an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Observe one injector result and its elapsed time.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Time the first invocation while capturing its output, then reuse that result for classification and size reporting.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain refusal diagnostics and a meaningful single-fire latency measurement. This removes a redundant action, not additional data fields from the diagnostic report.

unknowns: Partial scope: supplied standalone hooks and helper implementations were assessed. Referenced hooks/hooks.json, hooks/claude-hook.sh, commands/* and other host adapters are absent; actual plugin registration, startup dispatch and cross-host continuation enforcement remain unresolved.

Hook and tool output may remain with the caller or enter a host request to its configured model provider. The supplied source does not establish provider identity, actual remote transmission, logging, retention or deletion.

Actual planning/transcript contents and invocation-time user approval are unavailable. Sensitive content in free text, paths, commands or errors is conditional; no specific credential collection can be established.

Durable planning files and ledgers have no specified retirement policy. Inactive cache expiry, crash-leftover cleanup, effective Windows ACLs, backups, filesystem synchronization and physical erasure are not established.

Research/search examples and analytics templates do not supply external service implementations, recipients or credential handling. Their task-specific remote behavior cannot be inferred from these illustrations.
